T.thesis_one_line: America's big phone and fibre-internet company, priced as if its cash flow will shrink while it guides to growth and heavy buybacks.
key_adverse_facts: Pending $23B EchoStar spectrum purchase, originally expected to close in first half of 2026, still not closed at the Q2 2026 10-Q (0000732717-26-000297); leverage rises to about 3.0x.
H1 2026 FCF of 7.2B versus full-year guide of 18B+ requires 10.8B+ in H2.
Asset abandonment and impairment charges recur (286M in Q2 2026); goodwill plus licences about 45% of assets.
data_conflicts: Triage net debt/EBITDA 3.3x versus about 2.7x from 10-Q consolidated debt 143,954M less cash (company net debt 126.4B over TTM adjusted EBITDA about 47.2B); Yahoo total debt 165.8B includes leases.
Yahoo FCF 10.1B versus company FCF TTM about 16.3B (non-GAAP definition).
T.confidence_in_thesis: medium: guidance track record is clean (2025 beat) but the FCF guide is back-half loaded and EchoStar is unclosed; no V1 row to reconcile; insider and litigation detail not checked

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for T. Reverse DCF implies roughly -1.5% to -3% a year FCF growth versus a base of about +5% to 2028 (guide 18B, 19B, 21B).

T.scenario_basis: Start 2026 adjusted EPS guide 2.25-2.35 (mid 2.30), price 25.38; bear 2028 EPS 2.30 at 9x, base 2.65 at 11x, bull 2.85 at 12.5x; dividend 1.11 flat (4.4% yield) added to price CAGR.
kill_criteria: Net debt/adjusted EBITDA (consolidated, company definition) above 3.3x at any quarter-end after the EchoStar close, or no target-range path stated.
Full-year 2026 free cash flow guide cut below $18 billion, or reported FY2026 FCF below $17 billion.
Adjusted EPS 2026 guide cut below $2.25, or two consecutive quarters of adjusted EPS below $0.52.
Postpaid phone churn above 1.00% for two consecutive quarters (0.86% in Q2 2026).
EchoStar transaction not closed by 31 March 2027, or terminated.

CTSH.thesis_one_line: An IT-services firm that runs and rebuilds big companies' software, cheap because investors fear AI will shrink the hours clients buy.
key_adverse_facts: 2026 constant-currency revenue guide top end cut from 6.5% to 5.5% in the Q2 2026 release; Q2 2026 bookings fell 6% YoY.
Buybacks ($1.6B) and acquisitions ($1.3B) in H1 2026 exceeded H1 FCF of 657M; cash fell to 1,051M and $1.0B was drawn on the revolver.
India tax dispute: ITD asserts 33B rupees ($349M at 30 Jun 2026) on the 2016 share repurchase; new Project Leap restructuring costs $230-320M.
data_conflicts: d4/Yahoo shares 473M versus 450,444,209 on the 10-Q cover at 24 Jul 2026; market cap about 25.8B not 27.1B.
Triage said growth 4.5% and did not mention the bookings decline or Project Leap.
CTSH.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low: cheap and net-cash-neutral, but AI disruption is unquantifiable and bookings are slowing; no V1 row; Syntel and labor-code matters not read

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CTSH. Reverse DCF implies about -3% a year FCF growth for ten years versus a base of about +4%. [DV11 2026-10-09: with TTM SBC of $190M deducted (start FCF $2.41B) and cost of equity 8.84% (5.17% + 0.886 x 4.14%) the implied rate is about -2.7% to -3.0%; implied_vs_base stays below.]

CTSH.scenario_basis: Start 2026 adjusted EPS guide 5.70-5.82, price 57.33; bear 2028 EPS 5.30 at 9x, base 6.60 at 11x, bull 7.30 at 13x; dividend 1.32 (2.3% yield) added.
kill_criteria: Constant-currency revenue growth below 3.0% for two consecutive quarters (4.1% in Q2 2026).
Trailing-12-month bookings growth negative (5% in Q2 2026) or book-to-bill below 1.1x.
Full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guide cut below $5.63, the Q1 2026 low end.
Adjusted operating margin below 15.5% for any full year, or Project Leap costs above $320 million.
Consolidated net debt above $2.0B, or an adverse India Supreme Court/High Court ruling requiring cash payment above $349M.

PRU.thesis_one_line: A big US and Japan life insurer and asset manager, cheap, but its Japanese unit cannot sell new policies while regulators inspect it.
key_adverse_facts: Prudential of Japan new sales suspended through 5 Nov 2026 (extended by 180 days on 21 Apr 2026); estimated $525-575M pre-tax income reduction in 2026 and $400-450M in 2027; $50-60M a month if extended.
Japan FSA onsite inspections of Prudential of Japan and Prudential Holdings of Japan are ongoing; Gibraltar Life sales practices under review.
Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of 4.08 includes a 0.15 favourable annual-assumption benefit; retirement earnings flat.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q05) listed no red flags and did not mention Japan; it attributed EPS growth to a soft comp.
d4 shares 345M versus 348.1M Q2 2026 diluted weighted shares; immaterial.
PRU.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium: valuation is undemanding, but the Japan regulatory outcome is binary and the pre-extension cost estimate could not be verified

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for PRU. Reverse DCF on 3.0B of annual distributions implies about +1.6% a year growth versus a base of +4-5%; verdict is WATCH because of Japan event risk, not valuation.

PRU.scenario_basis: Start TTM adjusted EPS 15.25 and 2026 consensus about 14.5-14.9, price 119.45; bear 2028 EPS 13.50 at 7.5x, base 16.50 at 8.5x, bull 18.00 at 9.5x; dividend 5.60 (4.7% yield) added.
kill_criteria: Prudential of Japan new-sales suspension extended beyond 5 Nov 2026 by more than 90 days (cost $50-60M pre-tax a month).
Japan FSA imposes a business improvement or suspension order on Gibraltar Life or a group Japanese entity, or a stated ESR for any Japanese life subsidiary falls below the company's target.
Quarterly adjusted operating EPS below $3.30 (the Q4 2025 level) for two consecutive quarters excluding identified assumption updates.
Parent company highly liquid assets below $3.0B (4.2B at 30 Jun 2026) or share repurchases cut below the $250M a quarter pace.
PICA RBC ratio below 375% at any statutory year-end (415% at 31 Dec 2025).
